summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, chronic systolic heart failure, and atrial fibrillation was re-admitted for chest pain and orthopnea following a recent dialysis session. He developed acute on chronic heart failure with mild to moderate pulmonary edema, as confirmed by chest X-ray. His symptoms were attributed to fluid overload rather than acute cardiac injury, with stable troponin levels. He was treated with diuretics and underwent hemodialysis, which improved his volume status and respiratory symptoms. His chest discomfort, likely due to heart failure and possibly reflux, resolved with treatment. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to adhere to fluid restrictions, continue dialysis, monitor weight, and manage comorbidities including diabetes, heart failure, and substance use.

Diabetes with renal manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
